request.args: Why does character-level tokenization, where each character becomes an integer instead of a GPT-2 byte-pair token, require the script to have all of Shakespeare as one raw text first? Show it on the script's stated outputs: files of ids for training and validation, plus a file holding the encoder, the decoder and related info. Do not cover how the file is downloaded or how the distinct characters are found. Afterwards the reader should be able to say in one sentence what the script produces and why getting the text comes first.

block.title: How character‑level tokenization creates the script’s output
block.body:
The script first loads Shakespeare as one continuous string so it can see every character in order.

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"title":"Character‑level tokenization flow","kind":"flow","nodes":[{"id":"raw","label":"Read full Shakespeare text","role":"process"},{"id":"map","label":"Map each character to an integer ID","role":"process"},{"id":"split","label":"Split IDs into train and validation sets","role":"process"},{"id":"save","label":"Write train.bin, val.bin and meta.pkl","role":"outcome"}],"edges":[{"from":"raw","to":"map"},{"from":"map","to":"split"},{"from":"split","to":"save"}],"highlightPath":["raw","map","split","save"]}}
```

From that string it builds a dictionary that assigns each distinct character a unique integer. It then replaces the whole text with the corresponding sequence of IDs.

Next the ID sequence is divided into training and validation portions, and each part is saved as a binary file. Finally the encoder/decoder dictionaries and other metadata are written to a pickle file.

Thus the script produces three files – train.bin, val.bin, and meta.pkl – because the full raw text must be available to create a complete, ordered integer mapping before any splitting can occur.

questions.text: What happens if the text is read in chunks instead of as a whole?
How are the encoder and decoder dictionaries stored in meta.pkl?
Can the same process be used for other languages or corpora?
